cases.scope: Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise TCP-01, TLS-01 and HTTP-01 style attempts against scripted transports that perform a known sequence of DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP operations on a deterministic clock, each stage carrying synthetic raw-traffic canaries (DNS message bytes, TCP payload, TLS ClientHello/ServerHello bytes, HTTP header values and body bytes). Assert the observations array follows the injected execution order, omits stages that were never attempted, and stays within the registered observation and encoded-size limits; assert each serialized observation carries only the registered common fields (type, status, duration_ms, failure, details) and the registered details schema for its type, and that no canary byte sequence appears anywhere in the serialized result. Reject decoding of a synthetic observation that adds an unregistered field carrying raw bytes, a debug-log string or a censorship classification label. Assert the measurement outcome comes only from the registered test outcome rules, with no observation-level verdict. Requirements: REQ-OBS-0001, REQ-OBS-0002.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Measurement interpretation reviewer (analyst role independent of the implementer). Reviewed artifact: Go observation types, exported documentation and host/analyst guidance for measurement observations at the reviewed implementation revision. Checklist: (1) Does the documentation describe observations as normalized, bounded stage records of one Measurement Result rather than packet traces or debug logs? (2) Does no exported API, type name or doc comment present an observation as an independent censorship classification? (3) Does the guidance state that the registered test, not the observation, defines how observations determine the test-specific outcome? (4) Are any documented diagnostic or logging paths kept separate from observation output and free of raw traffic? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise sequential arrival indexes, quantized timing, closed normalized rcode values and bounded answer/CNAME counts.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test canonical A/AAAA/CNAME values, first-occurrence deduplication, TTL omission, reviewed-query limits and no on-device enrichment.
Synthetic core contract cases; Map each TCP failure conservatively and keep outer cancellation/network/proxy/deadline conditions exclusively in execution.reason.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise tcp_connect observations from a scripted transport for synthetic IPv4 (192.0.2.10) and IPv6 (2001:db8::10) destinations on synthetic port 8443, for succeeded and failed (connection_refused, timeout) operations. Assert details contains exactly address_family with ipv4 or ipv6 matching the attempted destination family, and that neither the destination address in any textual or byte form nor the port number appears anywhere in the serialized observation or result. Iterate decoder inputs and reject: details without address_family, address_family values unknown, IPv4, ipv4-mapped and empty string, and details carrying an extra address or port field. Accept the two valid values. Requirements: REQ-OBS-0017, REQ-OBS-0018.

Synthetic core contract cases; Drive a scripted transport through synthetic TCP and TLS stages and assert the serialized observation list. Iterate every registered tls_handshake failure value (timeout, connection_reset, alert, protocol_error, certificate_untrusted, certificate_name_mismatch, certificate_time_invalid, alpn_no_overlap, inconclusive): each yields a tcp_connect observation with status succeeded followed by one tls_handshake observation with status failed and that exact failure value. Reject an unregistered failure string (for example tls_reset) in a tls_handshake observation at validation. Inject a TCP-stage failure (timeout, then connection_refused) and assert it is emitted only as a preceding tcp_connect observation with status failed and the TCP failure value, with no tls_handshake observation present because TLS activity never began. Inject a successful TCP connect followed by cancellation before any TLS bytes are written and assert no tls_handshake observation is emitted. Requirements: REQ-OBS-0019, REQ-OBS-0020.
Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise conditional negotiated fields with closed version/ALPN/alert vocabularies and bounded ALPN; exclude every prohibited certificate/handshake/key/session field.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test registered HTTP failures and preceding DNS/TCP/TLS observations; emit HTTP only once HTTP activity starts.

Synthetic core contract cases; Construct synthetic http_exchange observations and validate their details object against the public table. Required fields: omit address_family or protocol and assert rejection; iterate address_family over ipv4, ipv6 and unknown and protocol over http/1.1, h2 and unknown and assert acceptance, and reject out-of-vocabulary values (for example h3). Conditional fields: status_code accepted only as an integer valid HTTP status code and absent when no valid status was received; redirect present only when at least one redirect was observed and only as a complete minimized redirect object; body present only when body processing began and only as a complete body summary; content_encoding accepted only as identity, unsupported or unknown. Checks count: accept a checks array of 17 entries (one status, 8 header, 8 body) and reject 18 entries, a second status check, a ninth header check and a ninth body check; assert checks is absent when no checks were configured. Requirements: REQ-OBS-0025.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test redirect counts/classes including uncontacted rejected redirects; exclude full destination data.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise HTTP-01 against a scripted HTTP server on a deterministic clock with identity-encoded synthetic bodies carrying canary bytes, using the registered terminal-body bound of 4,096 bytes (default) and a configured 65,536 bytes (maximum). Iterate body lengths 0, 4,095, 4,096 and 4,097 under the default bound and 65,535, 65,536 and 65,537 under the maximum. Assert bytes_processed is non-negative and never exceeds the configured bound, equals the full body length when the body completed within the bound with truncated false, and equals the bound with truncated true when the bound stopped processing before the body completed (the exactly-at-bound case follows the public table). Configure a synthetic expected body digest and assert only the check result (kind body, index, matched) is reported, while the body bytes, the computed digest and the expected digest are absent from the serialized result. Reject decoding of a body object with bytes_processed above the configured bound, negative bytes_processed, missing truncated, or an extra body-content or digest field. Requirements: REQ-OBS-0028, REQ-OBS-0029.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test kind/index/matched associations without retaining expected or actual header/body/digest values.

Synthetic core contract cases; Test that vocabularies are closed with no runtime registry lookup; decoders reject aliases, wrong case, numeric strings and raw library messages without repairing them into coarse markers; keep missing evidence, malformed data and out-of-subset values distinct.

Synthetic core contract cases; Map each effective code 0-5 and an out-of-subset code including extended bits; omit responses without a reliable code; exclude raw codes/diagnostics; keep OTHER distinct from success/no-data and map unregistered nonzero codes conservatively to inconclusive.

Synthetic core contract cases; Map negotiated 0x0303/0x0304/other versions and http/1.1, h2, dot and other negotiated ALPN; absent fields when nothing reliable was negotiated; ignore record-layer/offered versions; never copy unregistered identifiers or let coarse markers override failures.
Synthetic core contract cases; Accept only offered http/1.1, h2 and dot; reject unknown, h2c, case variants and other registry entries alongside existing count, length and duplicate bounds.

Synthetic core contract cases; Map every listed received peer description code and an unlisted code; omit alert when the description is unavailable; exclude local cancellation, deadline, validation failures, sent alerts and post-handshake closure; serialize no raw alert data.
Synthetic core contract cases; For each observation type, omit failure on incomplete status and reject null, empty or registered failure values; keep termination in execution.reason.

Synthetic core contract cases; Parameterize each invariant, including one terminal failed/incomplete primitive observation, allowed types, bounds, status/detail consistency and inconclusive for unmapped raw errors.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise a scripted TLS-01 style attempt where the TCP connect succeeds and the TLS handshake then fails with injected failures (timeout, alert, certificate_untrusted). Assert the serialized observations are exactly a succeeded tcp_connect followed by one failed tls_handshake carrying the injected registered failure, that the result records the terminal outcome registered by the test rather than any additional field naming a cause, actor or intent, and that the output is byte-identical whether the scripted failure is labelled as a synthetic outage or a synthetic interference scenario. Requirements: REQ-OBS-0033.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Measurement interpretation reviewer (analyst role independent of the implementer). Reviewed artifact: Go result documentation, examples and downstream analyst guidance describing stage-ordered observations at the reviewed implementation revision. Checklist: (1) Does each example of a failed later stage after a successful earlier stage claim only that the earlier stage completed and the later stage did not complete normally under that test configuration? (2) Does no example or guidance attribute intent, an actor or definitive interference to an observation order or stage failure? (3) Does the guidance list non-censorship explanations (for example outages, congestion, routing, server or CDN failures, proxy behavior) for stage failures? (4) Does the guidance recommend repeated measurements or independent observations before stronger conclusions? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.
Synthetic core contract cases; Feed negative DNS/TCP/TLS/HTTP terminal observations; produce completed measurements without automatic retries.
Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise required/conditional fields, encoded bytes/observation counts and task_id association. Exclude automatic task-field copies and reversible input digests.

Synthetic core contract cases; Inject a controlled random source; new runs get independent IDs, retries preserve ID/increment attempt, retransmission creates no attempt, and IDs never escape to measurement/context/log sinks.
Synthetic core contract cases; Select exact registered test/result-version tuples independently; reject unknown fields and unsupported combinations.
Synthetic core contract cases; Validate bounded released version and platform enum; exclude host/device/build/locale metadata and arbitrary annotations.
Synthetic core contract cases; Use a monotonic fake clock plus wall-clock jumps; test minute floor, 250ms ceiling including zero, stage rounding and duration_capped conditional behavior.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise all states/reasons, first termination precedence, measurement presence/absence/partial rules and separation of malformed task errors from results. Interrupt an attempt before and after its test starts and assert not_run before it and incomplete after it (REQ-RESULT-0051), and interrupt it after the test records its terminal outcome and assert the result stays completed with an unchanged state, reason and measurement (REQ-RESULT-0052).

Synthetic core contract cases; Test completed/incomplete remote tests with unavailable egress and NET-01 exceptions; reject network_context in every not_run result, including one whose snapshot was captured before it stopped (REQ-RESULT-0053); reject prohibited context data.
Synthetic core contract cases; Select the registered Output schema, ordered observation list and terminal outcome; reject unregistered extensions/verdicts.
Synthetic core contract cases; Interrupt each stage of NET-05 and primitive tests; retain only schema-permitted partial data and distinguish skipped from failed operations.

Synthetic core contract cases; Reject unknown known-version fields and unsupported exact versions; quarantine, if provided, cannot analyze a silently reduced object. Reject host/task injected extensions.

Synthetic core contract cases; Parameterize all common validity rules, including all-zero/incorrect run IDs, retry bound, timestamps, duration cap, terminal outcomes and prohibited data before bundling.

Synthetic core contract cases; Inject distinct synthetic canaries through the fake platform, host configuration and scripted transports for every prohibited class: person, account, application-user, advertising, device, SIM, subscriber, push and stable installation identifiers; task input and label values; raw packets, HTTP bodies, HTTP header values, certificate chains, cookies, credentials, system log lines, stack traces (from an injected internal panic) and unrelated resolver state. Run completed, incomplete and not_run attempts and assert no canary, in raw or base64url/hex form, appears in the serialized Measurement Result. Assert the result for a completed negative outcome (for example a TCP timeout) contains only the registered outcome and observations, and reject decoding of a result carrying an unregistered top-level field holding a synthetic derived anomaly or interference analysis object. Requirements: REQ-RESULT-0035, REQ-RESULT-0045, REQ-RESULT-0046, REQ-RESULT-0047, REQ-RESULT-0048, REQ-RESULT-0049, REQ-RESULT-0050.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Privacy and measurement interpretation reviewer (independent of the implementer). Reviewed artifact: Go result documentation, host integration guidance and analyst guidance for Measurement Results at the reviewed implementation revision. Checklist: (1) Does the guidance state that coarse platform, time, Network Context, connection code, task and run metadata can become identifying in combination and require bounded retention and aggregate reporting? (2) Does the guidance state that a matching task or run identifier establishes only measurement workflow membership, not that results belong to one person? (3) Does the guidance describe a completed negative outcome as one observation on one path and context that does not prove censorship or identify intent? (4) Does the guidance require derived anomaly or interference analysis to remain separate from the source result, identify its method and version, and preserve links to the source observations? (5) Is any documented retention or export path for results bounded and free of per-person aggregation? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise context capture with a fake platform that reports access-network generation G1, then switches to generation G2 during the attempt, and a fake egress endpoint, for both direct and proxy selected paths. Assert the result carries exactly one Network Context with one access object taken from the attempt's snapshot (network_changed true after the injected switch) and an egress object whose network_path equals the selected path, with no second access snapshot or path. Inject canaries for the public egress address (203.0.113.7, 2001:db8::7), local addresses (192.168.0.2, fe80::2) and persistent network identifiers (a synthetic platform network handle and generation token) and assert none appears in the serialized context. Reject decoding of a context carrying any additional address or identifier field. Requirements: REQ-CONTEXT-FORMAT-0001.

Synthetic core contract cases; Iterate synthetic Network Context JSON under the strict decoding contract: accept an object with valid access and egress objects, including egress status unavailable with lookup_source none; reject objects with access missing, egress missing, either set to null or to a non-object, and objects with one additional unknown top-level field. Assert every encoded context produced by the library, including when egress lookup fails, contains both access and egress and no other top-level key. Requirements: REQ-CONTEXT-FORMAT-0002, REQ-CONTEXT-FORMAT-0003.

Synthetic core contract cases; Iterate every registered access value and accept each: network_type wifi, cellular, ethernet, other, unknown; vpn_state detected, not_detected, unknown; ipv4_available, ipv6_available and validated yes, no, unknown; network_changed true and false. Reject case variants (WIFI, Yes), unregistered strings, network_changed as the string false or as null, and objects missing each required field in turn. Configure the fake platform to expose canaries for interface names, addresses, Wi-Fi identifiers, DNS server addresses, cell information, SIM information, carrier names, subscriber identifiers and location, and assert none appears in the encoded access object or result; reject decoding of an access object carrying any extra field for those items. Requirements: REQ-CONTEXT-FORMAT-0004, REQ-CONTEXT-FORMAT-0005.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test all status/source/path/connection-code/classification combinations, missing optional classification, and no guessed values.

Synthetic core contract cases; Configure the fake egress endpoint and fake platform to return a synthetic provider organization name and a synthetic mobile operator/carrier name as canaries alongside a valid asn. Assert the encoded Network Context contains only the registered numeric asn and no provider or operator text in any field, and reject decoding of a context carrying a provider or operator field at the top level, in access or in egress. Requirements: REQ-CONTEXT-FORMAT-0010, REQ-CONTEXT-FORMAT-0011, REQ-CONTEXT-FORMAT-0012.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Privacy and measurement interpretation reviewer (independent of the implementer). Reviewed artifact: Go Network Context documentation, analyst guidance and any proposed format extension touching provider or operator data at the reviewed implementation revision. Checklist: (1) Does any guidance on deriving a provider organization from asn name a documented mapping dataset? (2) Does the guidance present a derived provider label as contextual rather than a verified access-provider identity? (3) Is mobile operator information absent from the baseline implementation and documentation? (4) If an operator extension is proposed, does it record separate consent, platform, privacy, safety and legal review before adoption? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.
Synthetic core contract cases; Use normalized required fields and country eligibility only; reject region/ASN/provider/operator task allowlists.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test schema-permitted context carriage/deduplication and reject persistent cross-batch identity or listed private details.
Synthetic core contract cases; Mutate each field/conditional relationship; invalid context satisfies no execution requirement and is never attached as valid.
Synthetic core contract cases; Group valid individual results with a single-use bundle ID; rotating correlation is separate and default-off.

Synthetic core contract cases; Build bundles with linkage disabled (default configuration and an explicit disable) from a synthetic not_run TCP-01 result with reason constraints_unsatisfied and from a completed result. Assert the encoded bundle has exactly the top-level keys schema_version, bundle_id and results, with the linkage key absent (not null and not an empty object), and that the public disabled-linkage example decodes successfully. Reject decoding of a disabled-linkage bundle that carries linkage as null or an empty object, per the strict decoding contract. Requirements: REQ-BUNDLE-0003.
Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise envelope required fields/types, 1..16 results and encoded-byte bound; reject unknown fields.

Synthetic core contract cases; Inject random IDs; exact retries preserve identity/content, any membership/content mutation gets a new ID, acknowledgement/expiry deletes state, and no ID enters measurement traffic or targeting.
Synthetic core contract cases; Validate the exact complete rotating-installation object and local scope, encoded token/epoch, no stable mode or user_id representation.
Synthetic core contract cases; Bundle mixed completed/negative/not_run/incomplete attempts without changing semantics or adding unregistered context references.

Synthetic core contract cases; Fault-inject validation, persistence, ambiguous delivery and durable acknowledgement; replay identical logical bundles and delete by acknowledgement/expiry, never mutating linkage on retry.
Synthetic core contract cases; Parameterize ID/all-zero/encoding/count/size/result-schema/linkage/state/pending-storage invariants before submission.

Synthetic core contract cases; Assert a bundle built under the default configuration omits linkage. Inject canaries through the fake platform and host for advertising IDs, vendor IDs, device serials, hardware IDs, push tokens, account IDs, email addresses, phone numbers, SIM and subscriber identifiers and host application user IDs, plus hashed forms of each, and assert none appears in the encoded bundle. With linkage enabled, record all measurement traffic (DNS queries, TCP and TLS payloads, HTTP request lines, headers and bodies, HTTP CONNECT requests) and all Network Context endpoint requests, and assert neither bundle_id nor linkage.token appears in raw or base64url form. Run the same task set with linkage disabled, enabled with token T1 and enabled with token T2 and assert the delivered and executed task set is identical. Derive tokens from two different synthetic random installation secrets with identical host and platform identifiers and assert the tokens differ, and from one secret with different host and platform identifiers and assert the token is unchanged. Requirements: REQ-BUNDLE-0018, REQ-BUNDLE-0029, REQ-BUNDLE-0030, REQ-BUNDLE-0031, REQ-BUNDLE-0032, REQ-BUNDLE-0033, REQ-BUNDLE-0034, REQ-BUNDLE-0035, REQ-BUNDLE-0036.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Privacy and collector-operations reviewer (independent of the implementer). Reviewed artifact: Go bundle and linkage documentation plus host and collector integration guidance at the reviewed implementation revision. Checklist: (1) Does the collector guidance require linkage tokens to be treated as sensitive pseudonymous data rather than anonymous data? (2) Does the guidance advise against retaining source IP address, precise arrival time or transport logs together with a linkage token, and recommend separating transport handling from research storage where feasible? (3) Does the guidance require raw-token access to be restricted, audited and limited in retention? (4) Does the analysis and publication guidance require aggregation of linkage, time, region, ASN, network type and connection_code combinations? (5) Does the documentation state that hashing a host or platform identifier does not make it acceptable as a token source? (6) Does no documented host or collector path use linkage for task selection or delivery? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise bundle construction with a fake clock, fake secure storage and a synthetic installation secret: two bundles with the same secret, scope and epoch carry matching tokens; then trigger each locally reproducible cause in turn (linkage disabled, epoch rotation, explicit privacy reset, application data clearing via empty storage, key loss and storage failure via fake storage errors) and assert the token is absent or changed while the bundle schema is otherwise unchanged, with no added field or counter marking a new installation, person or account. Requirements: REQ-BUNDLE-0019, REQ-BUNDLE-0020.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Measurement interpretation reviewer (analyst role independent of the implementer). Reviewed artifact: Go linkage documentation and analyst guidance with correlation examples at the reviewed implementation revision. Checklist: (1) Do the examples treat matching tokens only as the same locally stored installation secret, deployment scope and rotation epoch? (2) Does no example claim that matching tokens identify the same person, device owner, account, physical location or access network? (3) Does the guidance list disabled linkage, epoch rotation, data clearing, reinstall detection, key loss, storage failure, device migration and privacy reset as causes of a missing or changed token? (4) Does no example count a missing or changed token as a new person? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.
Synthetic core contract cases; Recheck constraints immediately before attempts and preserve selected registered protocol semantics through direct/proxy transport.

Synthetic core contract cases; Use a deterministic clock and a synthetic task with retry.max_attempts 2 and retry_on platform_suspended, with a fake constraint evaluator whose result is scripted per call. Assert the evaluator is invoked immediately before each execution attempt, including the retry attempt: script satisfied for attempt 1 (which ends with platform_suspended) and unsatisfied for attempt 2, and assert attempt 2 is delayed or skipped according to the schedule while attempt 1's result is unchanged. Script unsatisfied for the first attempt of a run and assert the run is delayed or skipped, never executed. Assert across all scenarios that the count of runs equals the count of schedule-due runs: constraint evaluation, delay or skip never increments the run counter or creates a new run identity. Requirements: REQ-EXECUTION-0003, REQ-EXECUTION-0004.

Synthetic core contract cases; Decode synthetic execution objects through the strict task decoder. Reject an execution object without limits. Accept limits as an empty object (registered defaults applied: max_duration_ms 30000, max_bytes_sent 32768, max_bytes_received 131072, max_connections 8) and assert omitted network_path decodes as direct. Accept network_path direct and proxy and reject any other value. Accept network, device and concurrency when absent or present as typed objects of their defined schemas, and reject each when supplied as a non-object (string, array, null) or with an unknown field. Reject an unknown top-level execution field. Requirements: REQ-EXECUTION-0005.

Synthetic core contract cases; Test direct default and proxy selection; deny each proxy precondition, snapshot one generation across NET-05, and inject each path failure while asserting zero direct fallback.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise an accepted task with limits max_duration_ms 30000, max_bytes_sent 32768, max_bytes_received 131072 and max_connections 8 on a deterministic clock and scripted transport, with a retry bound permitting a second attempt of the same run. In attempt 1 consume exactly 8 connections, 32,768 application bytes sent and 131,072 received and terminate it with a cross-cutting reason that the public retry rules make retryable. Assert attempt 2 (same run_id, attempt 2) starts with full budgets: it can open 8 connections and send and receive the full byte limits, a 9th connection or one byte beyond either byte limit stops it with resource_limit, and its duration deadline is measured from its own start rather than from attempt 1. Requirements: REQ-EXECUTION-0011.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise omitted defaults, lower positive requests and above-local/registered rejection; count bytes at the transport boundary, including HTTP headers, DNS messages and length prefixes, stop reads and writes promptly at the counted limits and document buffering below that boundary.

Synthetic core contract cases; Configure the fake platform so required network information is unavailable: network_type unknown with allowed_transports [wifi, cellular], vpn_state unknown under vpn_policy exclude and require, and context required_fields [country_code] with the egress classification unavailable. Assert for each case that no network operation is issued on the recording transport and the attempt does not run (not_run with constraints_unsatisfied for each undeterminable network condition, network_context_unavailable only for the missing required context field), and that unknown is never treated as satisfying a constraint. Assert the same task runs when the fake platform reports the required values. Requirements: REQ-EXECUTION-0031.

Synthetic core contract cases; Iterate allowed_transports [wifi], [cellular] and [wifi, cellular] against fake-platform network_type wifi, cellular, ethernet, other and unknown, and assert the task runs only when the reported type is in the list. Reject a task whose allowed_transports contains a value outside the initial list (wifi, cellular). Iterate vpn_policy any, exclude and require (and the omitted default any) against vpn_state detected, not_detected and unknown and assert run or do-not-run exactly per the public VPN eligibility table. Exercise require_validated true with validated yes, no and unknown, using the fake system method when available and the fake library internal check otherwise, and assert execution only on confirmed validation. Exercise context required_fields and allowed_country_codes with present, missing and non-matching values. Assert every do-not-run case issues no network operation. Requirements: REQ-EXECUTION-0016, REQ-EXECUTION-0017.

Synthetic core contract cases; Use a fake platform that reports VPN state as detected, not_detected or unknown and evaluate each vpn_policy value (any, exclude, require) for all nine combinations. Expected: any runs for detected, not_detected and unknown; exclude runs only for not_detected and does not run for detected or unknown; require runs only for detected and does not run for not_detected or unknown. Assert omitted vpn_policy behaves as any. Assert the unknown state is carried through evaluation as unknown and is never mapped to not_detected, so exclude with unknown does not run. Reject an unregistered vpn_policy value (for example prefer) at validation. Requirements: REQ-EXECUTION-0018, REQ-EXECUTION-0019, REQ-EXECUTION-0020.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise required_fields/allowlists, missing/invalid/unknown context, optional context failure and stricter policy. Count requests to prove no endpoint/path override by tasks.
Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise battery/charging constraints using synthetic platform state, with local policy stricter than task values.

Synthetic core contract cases; Schedule synthetic tasks on a deterministic clock with scripted transports that record start and end times: two shared tasks S1 and S2 and one exclusive task E, submitted in the orders S1,S2,E and E,S1,S2 and with E submitted while S1 is running. Assert S1 and S2 may overlap, that E's execution interval never overlaps any other measurement's interval, and that no shared task starts while E is active. Assert that when E cannot run alone it either waits or ends not_run per the public constraint-evaluation rules, without starting any network operation while another measurement is active. Requirements: REQ-EXECUTION-0027.
Synthetic core contract cases; Independently fail every applicable runtime constraint and local/OS/user veto; no measurement starts.

Synthetic core contract cases; Register two synthetic local test implementations with the same test_id and different test_version values whose input schemas define different fields (version A requires field a, version B requires field b). Submit a task for version A with input containing a and assert acceptance; submit the same input under version B and assert rejection; submit input containing b under version A and assert rejection as an unknown field. Assert schema selection uses the exact (test_id, test_version) pair: an unregistered test_version, or an unregistered test_id with otherwise valid input, is rejected as a task-validation failure. Assert the generic task decoder accepts input only as an object and defines no input fields of its own. Requirements: REQ-INPUT-0001.
Synthetic core contract cases; Remove the locally registered input schema and make a fake schema downloader fail if called; reject before scheduling with zero network calls.

Synthetic core contract cases; Decode otherwise valid synthetic tasks through task admission, varying only the top-level `input` value. Accept `input: {}` for NET-01, whose registered input schema accepts an empty object, and assert the task is admitted. Reject `input: {}` for DNS-01, whose registered input schema requires `hostname` and `record_type`, with a bounded non-measurement admission error. For both NET-01 and DNS-01, iterate the non-object values `null`, `[]`, `[{}]`, `""`, `"{}"`, `0`, `1.5`, `true` and `false` as top-level `input`, and assert each is rejected at admission with a non-measurement admission error, no run or attempt is created and no Measurement Result is emitted. Verify a DNS-01 task with `input: {"hostname": "example.org", "record_type": "A"}` decodes to a JSON object value. Requirements: REQ-INPUT-0003, REQ-INPUT-0004.

Synthetic core contract cases; Parameterize required/type/empty/string/array/range/protocol/normalization/additional-field constraints from a registered schema. Exercise encoded-byte boundary and missing required subject without environment defaults.

Synthetic core contract cases; Inject each listed input failure independently, including an unavailable schema and denied target; reject before scheduling, return a task error and emit no measurement.
Synthetic core contract cases; Repeat normalization with equivalent supported inputs; reject ambiguous subject changes. Preserve only the normalized fields allowed by the exact Output schema.

Synthetic core contract cases; Use syntactically valid but unregistered/prohibited local, private, link-local and credential-bearing targets. Recheck redirects before contact; count zero contacts to denied destinations.
Synthetic core contract cases; Attempt every prohibited sensitive input class using synthetic canaries; verify no runtime substitution or automatic access to host/device data.
Synthetic core contract cases; Reject an unregistered generic hostnames array; exercise the exact registered array item/count/encoded-size boundaries for any supported multi-target schema.
Synthetic core contract cases; Construct output from a task containing canary inputs; retain only fields authorized by the selected Output schema and local policy.
Synthetic core contract cases; Try to widen input schemas or weaken local restrictions using task input; verify the registered schema and stricter local policy prevail.

Synthetic core contract cases; Execute the same synthetic task against a recording transport and deterministic clock twice, once with labels {"campaign": "a"} and once with labels {"campaign": "b", "measurement_group": "baseline"}. Assert identical network operations, schedule due times, execution-constraint decisions, limits and safety-policy outcomes; only the labels carried through to output may differ. Supply labels whose keys resemble typed control fields (for example network_path with value proxy, max_runs with value 28, vpn_policy with value require) and assert the typed execution and schedule values remain those of the typed fields, with no behavior change. Requirements: REQ-LABEL-0001, REQ-LABEL-0002.

Synthetic core contract cases; Decode synthetic tasks with labels omitted and with labels {} and assert they are equivalent in the decoded task and in downstream behavior. Accept a flat object with string keys and string values (for example {"campaign": "x"}). Reject labels as an array, string, number or null, a nested object value, an array value, and non-string values (number, boolean, null). Requirements: REQ-LABEL-0003, REQ-LABEL-0004.
Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise 16 entries, 64-byte keys, 128-byte values and 2048 encoded bytes at/below/above bounds, counting JSON syntax and multibyte text.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test the exact key alphabet, initial character, case sensitivity, length, and equal/conflicting/escaped duplicate names.
Synthetic core contract cases; Reject an unknown barometer. key; accept a structurally valid unreserved key without assigning it control semantics.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test UTF-8 and case preservation, control-character rejection, wrong types, literal expression text and absence of automatic numeric/boolean coercion.

Synthetic core contract cases; Use synthetic canaries for every prohibited identifier/content class and interpolation request; preserve permitted literal-or-reject handling and stricter label removal/rejection policy.
Synthetic core contract cases; Vary every apparent behavior/destination label and verify execution is unchanged; accept unknown unreserved metadata and exclude labels from current results.
Synthetic core contract cases; Mutate each validity predicate independently; return task-validation errors without emitting measurements.
Synthetic core contract cases; Use identical task envelopes with different exact test versions; select each version-specific options schema without changing the outer execution envelope.

Synthetic core contract cases; Decode otherwise valid synthetic NET-01 and DNS-01 tasks through task admission, varying only `options`. Reject a task with the `options` member omitted, for both tests, with a bounded non-measurement admission error, even though every DNS-01 option property is optional. Accept `options: {}` for NET-01 (no test-specific options defined) and for DNS-01, and assert the DNS-01 effective configuration equals its documented defaults: `resolver_mode` `system`, `transport` `udp`, `collect_additional_responses` `false`. For both tests, iterate the top-level values `null`, `[]`, `[{}]`, `""`, `"{}"`, `0`, `1.5`, `true` and `false` and assert each is rejected at admission with no run, attempt or Measurement Result created. Verify a DNS-01 task with `options: {"resolver_mode": "system"}` is accepted, so individual properties remain optional while the object is required. Requirements: REQ-OPTIONS-0003, REQ-OPTIONS-0004, REQ-OPTIONS-0005.

Synthetic core contract cases; Remove the local schema; parameterize required fields, types, defaults, enum/range/count/encoded-byte bounds and input relationships; reject unknown properties without network schema acquisition.
Synthetic core contract cases; Inject each listed unsupported, unavailable, inconsistent or out-of-envelope option case; reject before scheduling with no Measurement Result and no version fallback.
Synthetic core contract cases; Set a protocol timeout beyond the outer attempt deadline; exercise validation and outer cancellation without converting the outer interruption to a protocol outcome.
Synthetic core contract cases; Supply unsupported/unsafe explicit options and omitted defaults separately; observe rejection or permitted skipping without clamping, coercion or substitution.
Synthetic core contract cases; Attempt each listed option-based code/file/secret/interpolation/control-channel bypass; preserve registered behavior and stricter local safety policy.

Synthetic core contract cases; Admit a medium-risk synthetic task (registered baseline low) under a fake local policy that permits medium risk and schedules three attempts. Before each attempt change the trusted local inputs: attempt 1 permitted and started; attempt 2 with the local maximum lowered to low, not started; attempt 3 with the permission restored, started. Assert the declaration is evaluated before every attempt, not only at admission. Assert a fake host restriction can delay or skip an attempt even when every declared condition is satisfied. Count runs and attempts before and after each evaluation and assert none is created. Admission rows: a task declaring low risk with requires_user_consent false gains no permission over the same task declaring medium with consent required, and declaration fields cannot alter provenance, issuer authorization, target registration or policy. The per-attempt rows are execution-owned. Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0001, REQ-SAFETY-0002, REQ-SAFETY-0003.

Synthetic core contract cases; Use a synthetic registry with baselines low (NET-01) and medium (a synthetic medium-baseline test). For each baseline, declare low, medium, high and unknown with consistent risk_factors. Assert effective risk is never below the baseline: a low declaration on the medium baseline is rejected or evaluated as medium. Higher declarations raise effective risk to the declared level. Options or a schedule that a fake local assessment marks as increasing risk raise it further. Count runs and attempts with a fake scheduler before and after safety evaluation and assert evaluation adds none. Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0004, REQ-SAFETY-0005, REQ-SAFETY-0006.

Synthetic core contract cases; Validate the safety object field by field. Accept {risk_level: low, requires_user_consent: false} and the public complete example. Reject: missing risk_level; missing requires_user_consent; risk_level as 1, null, true or an array; requires_user_consent as "true", 1 or null; risk_factors as an object, a string or null; a risk factor given as a string; an unknown member in safety (risk_score) and in a factor (weight); and a duplicate member name. Each rejection is task_schema_invalid, produces no candidate and causes zero transport calls. Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0007.

Synthetic core contract cases; Admit synthetic NET-01 tasks (registered baseline `low`) under a fake local policy and deterministic clock, varying `safety.risk_level` with consistent `risk_factors` where required. Iterate `low`, `medium`, `high` and `unknown` and assert each is decoded as a supported value. Reject `none`, `""`, `"LOW"`, `"Unknown"`, `null`, `0` and a missing `risk_level` at admission with a bounded non-measurement admission error. Exercise `unknown` (with a `risk_factors` entry of level `unknown`) under a local policy with no unknown-risk permission and assert no execution attempt starts and no Measurement Result is produced (fail closed); repeat with a policy explicitly marked reviewed and permitting `unknown` and assert the run becomes eligible. Exercise `high` under a default policy and assert it is not executed, then under a reviewed policy explicitly permitting `high` and assert it becomes eligible. Assert no serialized task, admission status or result value represents a risk level of `none` or any risk-free value. Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0008, REQ-SAFETY-0009, REQ-SAFETY-0010, REQ-SAFETY-0011.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Safety and privacy reviewer (independent of the implementer). Reviewed artifact: Go public API documentation, host integration guidance and any host-facing risk-level descriptions at the reviewed implementation revision. Checklist: (1) Does any documentation or host-facing text describe a measurement or task as risk-free or as having no risk? (2) Is `low` described as a conservative classification under assessed deployment assumptions rather than a guarantee that execution is safe in every environment? (3) Is `unknown` documented as failing closed by default, runnable only under an explicit, reviewed local policy? (4) Is `high` documented as normally rejected unless explicitly permitted by a reviewed local policy? (5) Does guidance avoid presenting risk levels as guarantees to hosts or end users? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.

Synthetic core contract cases; Admit synthetic tasks under a fake local policy, varying `risk_level` and the presence of `risk_factors`. Accept `risk_level: low` with `risk_factors` omitted, and accept `low` with `risk_factors: [{"type": "network_observability", "level": "low"}]`. Reject `medium`, `high` and `unknown` each with `risk_factors` omitted, with a bounded non-measurement admission error and no run or attempt created. Reject `medium`, `high` and `unknown` each with `risk_factors: []` with the same bounded non-measurement admission error and no run or attempt created, and accept `low` with `risk_factors: []`. Accept `medium` with `[{"type": "traffic_distinctiveness", "level": "medium"}]`, `high` with `[{"type": "target_sensitivity", "level": "high"}]` and `unknown` with `[{"type": "data_sensitivity", "level": "unknown"}]` as structurally valid declarations (execution permission for `high` and `unknown` still depends on local policy). Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0012, REQ-SAFETY-0031.

Synthetic core contract cases; Admit synthetic tasks with `risk_level: unknown` (so every factor level is consistent) containing one risk factor, varying the factor object. Reject a factor missing `type` and a factor missing `level`, each with a bounded non-measurement admission error. Iterate factor `level` over `low`, `medium`, `high` and `unknown` and assert each is accepted; reject `none`, `""`, `"Medium"`, `null`, `1` and `true`. Iterate `type` over each initial registered type (`network_observability`, `traffic_distinctiveness`, `target_sensitivity`, `data_sensitivity`, `legal_or_social_context`) with `level: low` and assert each is accepted. Verify the decoded factor exposes exactly the `type` and `level` values supplied. Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0013, REQ-SAFETY-0014.

Synthetic core contract cases; With risk_level unknown and one factor of level unknown, iterate the five initial types and assert each is accepted and exposed unchanged. Submit unknown types (battery_drain, Network_observability, network-observability, an empty string and a 65-byte string) and assert each task is either rejected before scheduling with task_unsupported, never task_schema_invalid, or treated as unknown risk, and is never accepted with the factor ignored; the current validator rejects them, so admission must return task_unsupported. Submit execution concerns as factor types (bandwidth, battery, runtime, network_availability, device_state) and assert they are rejected as unknown types with task_unsupported, while the corresponding constraints in the execution object are accepted. Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0015, REQ-SAFETY-0016, REQ-SAFETY-0017, REQ-TRUST-0036.

Synthetic core contract cases; Iterate overall risk_level low, medium and high against a single factor at each of low, medium and high. Accept every pair where the overall level is at least the factor level, and reject low with medium, low with high and medium with high (overall with factor) as task_schema_invalid. Mixed factors low, medium and high are accepted under overall high and rejected under overall medium. With a factor of level unknown and no trusted local assessment, accept only overall unknown and reject low, medium and high. With a fake trusted assessment that resolves the unknown factor to medium, overall medium is accepted only through that trusted input, and the same bytes are rejected once the assessment is removed. Overall unknown with only known factors is accepted. Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0018, REQ-SAFETY-0019.

Synthetic core contract cases; Combine task requires_user_consent true and false with a fake host consent provider reporting valid, absent, expired and unavailable consent, and with the local consent requirement off and on. Task true with valid consent: an attempt may start. Task true with absent, expired or unavailable consent: no attempt starts and no Measurement Result is produced. Task false with the local requirement on and absent consent: no attempt starts. Task false with the local requirement off: no consent requirement is added, and risk and target checks still apply. Admission records the consent requirement as required when the task, issuer permissions or local policy requires it, and a task value of false never clears an issuer or local requirement. Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0020, REQ-SAFETY-0021, REQ-SAFETY-0022.

Synthetic core contract cases; Vary the registered baseline (low, medium), the task declaration (low, medium, high, unknown) and a fake local assessment (none, medium, high) independently. Assert effective risk equals the most restrictive of the three, with unknown dominating as unordered. Baseline medium with a low declaration is either rejected as invalid or admitted with effective risk of at least medium, and is never admitted as low. A high declaration on a low baseline gives effective risk high, and a local policy without high permission prevents execution. The admitted-task value exposes effective risk, and no task field lowers it. Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0023, REQ-SAFETY-0024, REQ-SAFETY-0025, REQ-SAFETY-0026.

Synthetic core contract cases; Start from a task meeting all five public safety conditions and assert an attempt may start. Deny one condition at a time: an invalid declaration, an unsupported factor, effective risk not permitted by local policy, invalid required consent, and a fake host or device restriction. For each assert no attempt starts, no Measurement Result or bundle entry is produced, and the outcome is a non-measurement admission error or a local not-run state distinct from every network failure reason. Make the safety assessment unavailable (a fake local assessor returning an error) and assert execution fails closed. Give the task unknown fields and labels that try to relax local privacy, consent or safety settings and assert nothing is relaxed. Assert rejection outputs carry no censorship, blocking or interference interpretation. Admission rows cover the declaration, factor support and effective-risk conditions; consent and host or device conditions are execution-owned. Requirements: REQ-SAFETY-0027, REQ-SAFETY-0028, REQ-SAFETY-0029, REQ-SAFETY-0030.

Synthetic core contract cases; Drive the scheduler with a deterministic clock and a fake platform that can report the application as suspended. Admit a NET-01 task with `starts_at` T and `not_after` T+24h. Keep the fake platform suspended from T-1h to T+2h and assert no attempt starts during suspension and the run is not marked failed or missed at T. On resume at T+2h assert the run becomes eligible and its attempt starts after T+2h, and assert the result `started_at` reflects the actual start, not `starts_at`. Repeat with suspension lasting until after `not_after` and assert no run or attempt starts after resume. Assert no API return value or status describes `starts_at` as a guaranteed or exact execution time. Requirements: REQ-SCHEDULE-0001.
Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise omitted/present and conditional schedule fields, defaults, wrong types and unknown properties.

Synthetic core contract cases; Use a deterministic clock and a synthetic task with repeat.mode interval, interval 21600, jitter 300, max_runs 3, a not_after after the third due run and retry.max_attempts 2 with retry_on internal_error and backoff mode fixed, initial_delay_ms 30000, max_delay_ms 30000. Script attempt 1 of run 1 to end with internal_error and every other attempt to complete. Assert three distinct run identities, run 1 holding attempts 1 and 2 and runs 2 and 3 holding attempt 1 only, the run counter reaching 3 and attempt numbering scoped to each run. Assert a retry attempt shares its run identity and never creates a new run, and that each interval-due run receives a new run identity. With repeat.mode none and the same retry policy, assert exactly one run whose attempt count is at most 2. Requirements: REQ-SCHEDULE-0003, REQ-SCHEDULE-0004, REQ-SCHEDULE-0005, REQ-SCHEDULE-0006.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test before/at/after starts_at plus permitted null/absence; do not run early or require exact timing.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test acceptance/issuance-relative expiry at boundaries and the reviewed embedded one-time exception.

Synthetic core contract cases; Drive the scheduler with a deterministic clock and fake platform timezone UTC, admitting NET-01 tasks whose runs are otherwise eligible. With `time_window` `{"timezone": "local", "ranges": [{"start": "12:00", "end": "18:00"}]}`, advance the clock to local 11:59, 12:00, 17:59 and 18:00 and assert a run starts only at 12:00 and 17:59 (start inclusive, end exclusive) and not at 11:59 or 18:00. With the midnight-crossing range `22:00`-`06:00`, assert no start at 21:59 and 06:00 and a start at 22:00 and 05:59. With two ranges `08:00`-`10:00` and `14:00`-`16:00`, assert no start at 12:00 and a start at 14:00. Assert a run that becomes due outside the window is delayed to the next allowed range start before `not_after` rather than started early. Requirements: REQ-SCHEDULE-0012.

Synthetic core contract cases; Validate synthetic `time_window` objects at admission and evaluate accepted ones with a deterministic clock and a fake platform timezone. Reject `ranges` omitted and `ranges: []` (0 ranges), accept 1 range and 4 non-overlapping ranges (`00:00`-`02:00`, `04:00`-`06:00`, `08:00`-`10:00`, `12:00`-`14:00`) and reject 5 ranges, with a bounded non-measurement admission error. Reject two identical ranges `08:00`-`12:00`, overlapping ranges `08:00`-`12:00` and `11:00`-`14:00`, and a midnight-crossing overlap `22:00`-`06:00` with `05:00`-`07:00`. Accept `timezone` omitted and assert it is treated as `local`. Reject `timezone` values `UTC`, `Europe/Berlin`, `""` and `Local` with a bounded non-measurement admission error and no run or attempt created. With range `12:00`-`18:00` and `timezone: local`, set the fake device timezone to UTC at fixed instant 10:30Z (local 10:30, no start), then switch it to UTC+03:00 at the same instant (local 13:30) and assert a run starts, demonstrating `local` uses the current device-reported timezone. Requirements: REQ-SCHEDULE-0013, REQ-SCHEDULE-0014, REQ-SCHEDULE-0043.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test HH:mm syntax, inclusive start/exclusive end, midnight expansion and overlapping ranges after expansion.
Synthetic core contract cases; Distinguish none and interval, disallow interval-only fields for none and generate the bounded number of runs.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise interval/jitter bounds and delayed due runs with injected random offsets; offsets are locally generated per run and stay inside start/expiry/window constraints.
Synthetic core contract cases; Keep run identity/max_runs accounting stable across the second attempt; a terminal negative measurement creates no automatic retry.
Synthetic core contract cases; Enumerate permitted and forbidden reasons; exercise attempts=1/2 conditional fields, fixed/exponential delays and jitter at expiry and delay bounds.

Synthetic core contract cases; Decode synthetic schedules: omitted max_runs with repeat.mode none defaults to 1; max_runs 0 rejected, 1 accepted, 28 accepted, 29 rejected; non-integer max_runs rejected. With repeat.mode interval, omitted max_runs is rejected and max_runs 28 accepted. Execute with a deterministic clock, repeat.mode interval (interval 21600, jitter 300), max_runs 2, a valid not_after and retry.max_attempts 2 with retry_on platform_suspended and backoff mode fixed, initial_delay_ms 30000, max_delay_ms 30000, scripting a retry in run 1: assert two runs complete and the retry does not count toward max_runs. Configure max_runs 28 with a not_after reached after 2 runs, and separately max_runs 2 with a later not_after, and assert the schedule terminates at whichever limit is reached first. Requirements: REQ-SCHEDULE-0030, REQ-SCHEDULE-0031, REQ-SCHEDULE-0032.
Synthetic core contract cases; Mutate each listed schedule constraint; reject expired/invalid schedules, and redeliver identical tasks without extending expiry or adding schedules.
Synthetic core contract cases; Deny each eligibility predicate independently for initial and retry attempts; assert no early/out-of-window/expired execution and preserve stricter local veto.

Synthetic core contract cases; Submit synthetic tasks to admission with a recording result sink and deterministic clock: a valid NET-01 task, a task with invalid `input`, a task with an expired `not_after`, and a task carrying an extra top-level `results` member containing a canary result-like object. Assert the valid task is admitted and that admission alone writes zero Measurement Results to the sink; assert each invalid task returns a bounded non-measurement admission error and also writes zero Measurement Results. Assert the canary result content never appears in any later Measurement Result, log or status output, and that the only Measurement Result for the valid task is produced after its execution attempt. Requirements: REQ-TASK-0002.

Synthetic core contract cases; Decode a minimal supported task, then omit each required envelope field, add an unknown field, violate task identifier syntax/byte bounds and exceed the complete encoded-byte bound. Check campaign-wide identity is preserved and no result is decoded as task input.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Specification maintainer reviewer (independent of the change author). Reviewed artifact: Proposed task schema changes and their specification diffs at the reviewed specification revision. Checklist: (1) Does the proposal add a new top-level task field? (2) If a new top-level field is proposed, does the change record why the extension cannot be placed inside an existing nested object (`input`, `options`, `schedule`, `execution`, `safety` or `labels`)? (3) Are extensions that fit an existing nested object placed there? (4) Is the change frequency of the top-level schema kept rare, with the change recorded in the specification change history? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.
Synthetic core contract cases; Run multiple tests on one generation/path; acquire shared bounded context rather than independently repeating per test.

Synthetic core contract cases; Feed the Go core access context through a fake platform that also offers canary values for every forbidden item: interface name, local IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, DNS server address, SSID, BSSID, cell identifier, SIM information, subscriber identifier, carrier account information and physical location. Iterate `network_type` over `wifi`, `cellular`, `ethernet`, `other` and `unknown`, `vpn_state` over `detected`, `not_detected` and `unknown`, `ipv4_available`, `ipv6_available` and `validated` over `yes`, `no` and `unknown`, and `network_changed` over `true` and `false`. Assert the serialized access object contains exactly these six fields with the supplied normalized values. Assert serialized output of the access object, the Measurement Result, logs, cache entries and egress-endpoint requests contains none of the canary values. Reject an access input carrying any additional field. Requirements: REQ-CONTEXT-0002, REQ-CONTEXT-0003.

Synthetic core contract cases; Run synthetic attempts against a local synthetic classification endpoint that records the observed source address and returns `{"country_code": "NL", "region_code": "NL-NH", "asn": 64500, "classification_version": "0.1.0"}`. For a `direct` attempt, assert the egress object contains `status`, `lookup_source`, `network_path: direct`, the classification fields and `classification_version`, and no `connection_code`. For a `proxy` attempt through a scripted loopback CONNECT proxy with `connection_code` `outline_mobileproxy`, assert the lookup goes through the proxy and the egress object includes that `connection_code`. Configure the endpoint to additionally return a field carrying the observed source address and assert the response is rejected and egress reports `status: unavailable`. Assert the recorded source address never appears in serialized results, cache keys, logs or status output. Requirements: REQ-CONTEXT-0004, REQ-CONTEXT-0005, REQ-CONTEXT-0006.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Privacy reviewer and measurement interpretation reviewer (independent of the implementer and endpoint operator). Reviewed artifact: Egress-classification endpoint operating documentation and Go result documentation and analyst guidance for egress context at the reviewed revision. Checklist: (1) Does the endpoint operator documentation state that the source IP is classified without being returned and that its retention is minimized or avoided? (2) Is the endpoint logging configuration consistent with that minimization statement? (3) Does result and analyst guidance describe country and region as IP classification, not the user's physical location? (4) Does guidance state that ASN describes the observed egress network and may not identify the access operator, especially with VPN, proxy, carrier-grade NAT or circumvention paths? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.

Synthetic core contract cases; Validate endpoint URLs/fields/independent approvals, absence fallback to access-only, immutable configuration and rejection of redirects/discovery/credentials/per-user URLs.

Synthetic core contract cases; Capture one fixed HTTPS GET without identifier/target/category/cookie/auth data. Validate exact response schema, 4096-byte/5000ms limits, forbidden fields and successful unknown classifications.
Synthetic core contract cases; Run direct/proxy/NET-05 with generation changes; assert one matching snapshot and no direct request or cache substitution during proxy-only execution.

Synthetic core contract cases; Count primary/fallback calls, test valid-but-empty primary, malformed/TLS/HTTP/timeout/size failures, exact cache-key hits/misses, freshness and every invalidation event. Verify no persistent cache.

Synthetic core contract cases; Inject cancellation/deadline/suspension/network changes during acquisition; distinguish missing required context, allowlist mismatch and optional egress failure. Admission rejection row, while this build provides no egress acquisition (DEV-578): submit otherwise valid tasks that require country_code, region_code or asn individually, or a country allowlist, and assert each is rejected at admission as task_unsupported with zero transport calls, while tasks with an absent or empty context are admitted; this row is removed when acquisition is provided. Requirements: REQ-CONTEXT-0025, REQ-CONTEXT-0026, REQ-CONTEXT-0027, REQ-CONTEXT-0028, REQ-TRUST-0036.

Synthetic core contract cases; Configure a fake platform with canary device locale, timezone, language, SIM country, application store region and user-profile values, and a synthetic classification endpoint. With the endpoint returning only `{"classification_version": "0.1.0"}`, assert the egress object omits `country_code`, `region_code` and `asn` and no provider or operator value appears anywhere in serialized output, so nothing is inferred from the canaries. With the endpoint returning `asn` 64500, assert the ASN and `classification_version` are retained and no free-form provider name field is produced. Configure the endpoint to also return a free-form operator name and assert the response is rejected. Iterate `network_type` `wifi` and `cellular` and assert no mobile operator or SIM carrier field is collected. Requirements: REQ-CONTEXT-0029, REQ-CONTEXT-0030, REQ-CONTEXT-0031.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Measurement interpretation reviewer (analyst role independent of the implementer). Reviewed artifact: Analysis documentation describing ASN-to-organization mapping at the reviewed revision. Checklist: (1) Does analysis map ASN to an organization only using the recorded `classification_version` or another documented dataset? (2) Is the mapping dataset and its version documented for each analysis? (3) Is a mapped organization presented as contextual rather than as a verified access-provider identity? (4) Does any analysis derive provider or operator values from locale, timezone, language, SIM country, application store or user profile? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.

Synthetic core contract cases; Run synthetic attempts with canary installation, account, device and session identifiers, `task_id`, `test_id`, measurement target hostname, `connection_code`, cookies and a local address present in host and task state, against a recording classification endpoint. Assert each request is a single `GET` to the configured fixed URL with `Accept: application/json` and contains none of the canaries in path, query, headers or body, and carries no `Cookie` or `Authorization` header. Configure the endpoint to return a field carrying the observed IP address and assert the response is rejected. Feed fake platform canaries for GPS location, Wi-Fi identifiers, interface names, cell identifiers, SIM identifiers, phone numbers, subscriber identifiers and carrier account data and assert none appear in any serialized output. Assert a response without `region_code` is accepted with `region_code` absent. Assert that when `asn` is present no provider name field is emitted. Inject endpoint failure (unreachable primary and fallback) and assert egress reports `status: unavailable` with `lookup_source: none`, and the result carries no censorship-indicating outcome attributable to the failure. Requirements: REQ-CONTEXT-0032, REQ-CONTEXT-0035, REQ-CONTEXT-0036, REQ-CONTEXT-0037, REQ-CONTEXT-0038, REQ-CONTEXT-0039, REQ-CONTEXT-0040, REQ-CONTEXT-0041, REQ-CONTEXT-0042.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Privacy and safety reviewer (independent of the implementer and endpoint operator). Reviewed artifact: Host deployment configuration, endpoint privacy review records, endpoint operator logging configuration and public-reporting methodology at the reviewed revision. Checklist: (1) Are the configured primary and fallback endpoints each covered by a recorded privacy review? (2) Does the endpoint operator disable or minimize raw access logs and avoid combining source IP and request time with unrelated user or application data? (3) Does the deployed endpoint return only coarse classifications and never the observed IP address? (4) Is region collection enabled only where its necessity and reliability are documented? (5) Does public reporting aggregate context into sufficiently broad groups rather than raw combinations of region, ASN, network type, connection code and time? (6) Does reporting avoid treating endpoint or classification failure as evidence of censorship? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test normalized coarse Android/Apple adapter outputs and unsupported=unknown behavior; reject raw platform objects or sensitive transport details.

Synthetic core contract cases; Configure a scripted local proxy listener on `127.0.0.1` and accept the configuration `{"host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 54321, "connection_code": "outline_mobileproxy"}` with no test identifiers or test capability declaration. Run a TCP-01 proxy attempt and assert the library opens one TCP connection to the loopback endpoint and sends an HTTP/1.1 `CONNECT` request line for the target authority, and nothing else is used as proxy transport. Reject configurations adding a transport selector such as `"type": "socks5"`, a declared supported-tests list, or a non-loopback `host` such as `192.0.2.1`, leaving the previous configuration unchanged. Script the listener to reply with a SOCKS handshake reply or a non-HTTP/1.1 status line and assert the attempt fails per the public outcome table without direct fallback. Reject a DNS-01 task with `network_path: proxy` using UDP transport, which needs a non-stream capability. Requirements: REQ-PROXY-0001.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise the Go binding-facing initialization, replacement and clearing entry points using only ordinary serializable values: initialize with a proxy object {host "127.0.0.1", port 54321, connection_code "outline_mobileproxy"}, replace it with {host "127.0.0.1", port 55001, connection_code "outline_mobileproxy"}, then clear it. Assert after each call that the active configuration equals exactly the supplied object (or no proxy after clearing) and that a recording fake proxy listener receives new proxy-task tunnels only on the port of the current configuration. Run a concurrent reader during replacement and assert it observes either the complete previous or the complete new object, never a mixed host/port/connection_code combination, so replacement is atomic. Assert the exported initialization, setProxy-equivalent and clearProxy-equivalent signatures take only strings, integers and maps/JSON bytes, with no callback, interface, socket or object parameter. Initialize with both a proxy object and a separate top-level network_context object {primary_endpoint, fallback_endpoint} and assert both are configured independently; a proxy object carrying primary_endpoint or fallback_endpoint is rejected, and replacing or clearing the proxy leaves the configured egress endpoints unchanged. Requirements: REQ-PROXY-0002, REQ-PROXY-0003, REQ-PROXY-0004.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Mobile binding reviewer (independent of the binding implementer). Reviewed artifact: Android, Apple and Flutter binding source and integration documentation for proxy initialization, replacement and clearing at the reviewed revision. Checklist: (1) Do the Android, Apple and Flutter bindings accept the proxy only as ordinary serializable values (host, port, connection_code)? (2) Is the host free of any requirement to supply native callbacks, interfaces, sockets or complex objects to configure, replace or clear the proxy? (3) Does each binding's method naming map to initialization, atomic replacement and clearing with semantics equivalent to the Go core contract? (4) Do the bindings and documentation configure the egress-classification endpoints separately at initialization rather than as properties of the proxy object? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.
Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise loopback/localhost, port and connection_code boundaries and forbidden fields/transports; reject non-loopback endpoints.
Synthetic core contract cases; Attempt malformed replacement while an old proxy is active; preserve old state. Test category stability/privacy and internally derived compatibility.

Synthetic core contract cases; Race set/clear with attempts and all NET-05 steps; block old-generation admission, cancel/close and bound cleanup before returning, invalidate caches and never mix generations or use direct fallback.

Synthetic core contract cases; Capture synthetic CONNECT exchanges for explicit IP and hostname cases, 2xx/non-2xx/malformed/timeouts, redirects and cancellation. Assert exact authority, no credentials/cleartext target GET, fresh tunnels and unchanged TLS semantics.
Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise direct default and proxy preconditions; task cannot carry endpoint, category or proxy identity.
Synthetic core contract cases; Fail primary context endpoint and verify same-generation proxied fallback, exact cache keys and required-context gating with zero direct requests.

Synthetic core contract cases; Parameterize all nine registered tests and relevant input/options combinations, including each incompatible NET-05 step, on network_path: proxy. Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Measurement interpretation reviewer (analyst role independent of the implementer).
