Normalization: a form that the public rules normalize to the registered value matches, while a suffix (evil-example.test against example.test), a subdomain, a URL with an extra path prefix and an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address do not. Expiry one second after the fake clock is accepted; expiry at or before it is rejected. Registrations with URL credentials or interpolation syntax fail policy construction. Execution-owned rows: with a scripted resolver returning an unregistered address and a scripted redirect to an unregistered location, assert no connection to either. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0013, REQ-TRUST-0014, REQ-TRUST-0015, REQ-TRUST-0016.

Synthetic core contract cases; Instrument admission with a fake delivery-record store, clock, registry, policy, replay store and recording transport that log the order of calls. A valid task runs the eleven public steps in order, and its handle is returned only after the replay write commits. Build tasks that each fail exactly one step and assert the listed class: missing, expired, foreign-instance or byte-mismatched delivery record, task_source_unauthenticated; a remote task whose signed package fails verification, task_source_unauthenticated; unavailable trusted clock, task_trust_unavailable; a remote package issued 301 seconds after acceptance, task_source_unauthenticated, while 300 seconds is accepted; 65,537 bytes, task_limit_exceeded; unknown top-level field, task_schema_invalid; well-formed but unregistered test_version, task_unsupported; uppercase task_id, task_schema_invalid; 129-byte task_id, task_limit_exceeded; expired task, task_expired; execution.context requiring egress Network Context in a build without egress acquisition, task_unsupported; no installed policy, task_policy_unavailable; source policy_generation one above the active generation, task_policy_unavailable, and one below, policy_rollback; unknown issuer, task_issuer_not_authorized; a proxy task whose test, input or options are incompatible with HTTP CONNECT, task_schema_invalid; direct or proxy path not permitted by issuer authority or local policy, task_issuer_not_authorized; path not permitted by the matched target registration, and an unregistered target, target_not_registered; effective risk above the issuer maximum or a local-policy bound, and unknown risk without a reviewed local permission, task_issuer_not_authorized; replay conflict, task_id_conflict; replay write failure, task_trust_unavailable. For each assert exactly one class, that no later step's capability is called, that no replay or admitted-task record exists, that no handle is returned and that the transport, DNS and Network Context fakes see zero calls. Precedence follows the first failing step: an unknown top-level field with an unknown issuer returns task_schema_invalid (step 4 before 7), an unregistered test_version with a 129-byte task_id returns task_unsupported (step 4 before 5), an expired task with an unregistered target returns task_expired (step 6 before 8), a 65,537-byte task presented as remote without a signed package returns task_source_unauthenticated (step 2 before 3), and within step 8 invalid options with a proxy-incompatible test return task_schema_invalid with the compatibility rule not consulted, while a proxy-incompatible task whose path is not permitted by issuer or local policy, or by its matched registration, returns task_schema_invalid (compatibility before path authority and target registration). A valid task that requires egress context performs no context lookup during admission in a build that provides egress acquisition. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0046, REQ-TRUST-0018, REQ-TRUST-0047, REQ-TRUST-0039.

Synthetic core contract cases; Iterate task_id values: 1 and 128 bytes of allowed characters (lowercase ASCII letters, digits, ".", "_", "-") accepted; empty and 129 bytes rejected; uppercase, space, "/" and non-ASCII characters rejected, all before any network activity. Replay key: deliver the same task_id from two admitted issuers and assert both are accepted as distinct replay keys; deliver the same task_id from one issuer with identical bytes and assert idempotent redelivery, and with different bytes assert task_id_conflict. Campaign-wide identity: admit identical task bytes on two fake installations with different linkage tokens and assert each accepts the identical task_id and emits it unchanged in results, with no installation-specific rewriting or interpolation. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0019, REQ-TRUST-0020.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Task issuer campaign reviewer (independent of the task author). Reviewed artifact: Issuer task-generation procedure and a sample of issued campaign task definitions at the reviewed revision. Checklist: (1) Does each task_id identify one campaign task definition within the issuer namespace? (2) Is each task_id identical for every installation receiving the same task definition? (3) Is no task_id derived from a person, account, installation, device, advertising ID, push token, linkage token, IP address or other participant-specific value? (4) Is no task_id used to select an individual installation or reconstruct cross-bundle linkage? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise every replay-table row with a deterministic clock and fake persistent storage: a new replay key continues admission; the same key with identical bytes is idempotent redelivery with no duplicate runs and unchanged expiry; the same key with one changed byte (including whitespace only) is rejected as task_id_conflict; a lower policy generation than the active one is rejected as policy_rollback; an expired task is rejected as task_expired and never reactivated on later redelivery; unavailable or corrupted replay state fails closed with task_trust_unavailable for a remote task and, with the same storage fault injected, for an embedded task, which is never accepted, assigned a handle or made executable without replay state. Assert the persisted record contains only the (issuer_id, task_id) key, a SHA-256 digest equal to an independently computed digest of the exact accepted bytes, the accepted policy generation and acceptance/expiry classes with retention ending 86,400 seconds after task expiry, and that synthetic canary input, target, label, participant and result strings are absent from stored bytes. Post-clearing redelivery rows are planned separately in CC-TRUST-REPLAY-AFTER-CLEARING. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0021, REQ-TRUST-0022, REQ-TRUST-0023, REQ-TRUST-0024, REQ-TRUST-0038, REQ-LIMIT-0023.

Synthetic core contract cases; Submit synthetic tasks attempting recipient selection by linkage or installation token, bundle_id or run_id, account, advertising, device, SIM, subscriber or push identifiers, exact IP address or precise location, or prior per-installation outcomes, through any selector, label, eligibility or unknown field, and assert each is rejected at admission before network activity. Submit tasks whose task_id, labels, targets or payload contain placeholder syntax for deployment, application version, cohort, country or network values and assert the library performs no local interpolation: values stay literal or the task is rejected. With linkage disabled and with two different synthetic tokens, deliver the same task set and assert identical admission and scheduling decisions, with no token exposed to task-selection or host-policy hooks. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0026, REQ-TRUST-0027, REQ-TRUST-0028.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Host deployment policy reviewer (independent of the deployment operator). Reviewed artifact: Host task-eligibility policy and its reviewed criteria at the reviewed revision. Checklist: (1) Is eligibility limited to broad deployment, application-version, consented cohort, country or network criteria? (2) Are the criteria non-user-specific and the groups sufficiently broad? (3) Has the policy itself been reviewed and is that review recorded? (4) Does any deployment need participant-specific longitudinal research, and if so is it excluded from claims of compliance with this baseline? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.

Synthetic core contract cases; Initialize with policy generation 2 and admit a task. Assert from the root package source that only the replacement seam assigns the active policy, adapters or admitter, that admission leaves the active generation unchanged and that Initialize on an initialized client returns already_initialized. Drive replacement by quiesce and reinitialization with fault injection at each implemented step. Validation refuses generation 2 (equal) and 1 (lower), an incomplete policy, retained replay acceptances above the new generation, unavailable replay generations and a panicking trusted clock with policy_rejected. After quiescing, a panic while cancelling the current generation and a delivery store that refuses the new generation leave the client uninitialized, and reserved work outliving the lifecycle deadline leaves it blocked with cleanup_incomplete until close. After each validation failure assert the complete generation-2 policy, its handles and its delivery references stay active and its tasks still admit; after each later failure assert no policy remains and that a reinitialized client rejects generation-2 and generation-3 deliveries with task_policy_unavailable, never mixing registrations. Assert in-flight admission is cancelled with no replay record or handle. On a successful generation-3 replacement that removes the task's registration, assert the previous generation's context is cancelled, its task handles and delivery records no longer resolve, a generation-3 redelivery is rejected as target_not_registered and a generation-2 delivery as policy_rollback; after a generation-4 replacement restoring the registration, a redelivery resolves to the retained acceptance under a new handle, and after clearing, initializing generation 2 or 3 fails closed while generation 4 initializes. Send policy-shaped content through permitted task labels and unknown task members and assert the active generation, issuers and registrations are unchanged. Run concurrent replacements and admissions and assert one highest winning generation. Host authentication of policy updates, run cancellation, Network Context cache invalidation and collector, target, proxy and context endpoint paths are planned separately in CC-TRUST-LOCAL-POLICY-LIFECYCLE-RUNTIME. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0029, REQ-TRUST-0030, REQ-TRUST-0031, REQ-TRUST-0032.

Synthetic core contract cases; With the reviewed host policy adapter (DEV-455), run reservation (DEV-561) and Network Context caching (DEV-578) in place, reject a policy update whose authentication or integrity check fails before the replacement seam is called and assert the generation-2 policy stays active. On a generation-3 replacement that removes a registration, assert a queued and a running run of the affected task are cancelled before any generation-3 attempt starts and that no attempt continues under the removed registration. Populate access and egress Network Context snapshots under generation 2 and assert none is used by a generation-3 attempt. Return policy-shaped content from collector reply, target response, proxy and context endpoint fakes and assert the active generation, issuers and registrations are unchanged. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0029, REQ-TRUST-0030, REQ-TRUST-0031, REQ-TRUST-0032.

Synthetic core contract cases; Trigger each public class through a synthetic delivery: task_source_unauthenticated, task_issuer_not_authorized, task_policy_unavailable, task_trust_unavailable, task_expired, task_id_conflict, policy_rollback, target_not_registered, task_limit_exceeded, task_schema_invalid and task_unsupported. Trigger task_unsupported with three otherwise valid tasks: a well-formed but unregistered (test_id, test_version) pair, a risk factor type the build does not recognize and rejects, and an execution.context value requiring egress Network Context in a build without egress acquisition; assert none returns task_schema_invalid, and that with a fake build that provides egress acquisition the same egress task is admitted. Assert each returns a task.AdmissionError whose code is the expected class and whose text is the fixed class string, and that no Measurement Result, bundle entry or result-sink call is produced. Embed unique canaries in the task payload, a target URL, a label, a fake credential, verification-key and signature bytes in the delivery record, and the raw error text of a failing fake store and clock. Assert no canary appears in the error text, in %v or %+v formatting, in any errors.Unwrap chain or in captured log output. Assert repeating an identical failing delivery returns an identical error. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0033, REQ-TRUST-0034, REQ-TRUST-0035, REQ-TRUST-0036.

Synthetic core contract cases; Accept exactly one schema-typed JSON value with permitted whitespace; reject empty, BOM, extra values/content, comments, trailing commas and non-object roots for object schemas.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test malformed UTF-8, escapes and unpaired surrogates; accept valid scalar pairs and preserve distinct non-normalized/case-sensitive strings and member names.
Synthetic core contract cases; Reject equal, conflicting and escaped-equivalent duplicate names at every nesting level; allow same names in distinct objects and distinct Unicode scalar sequences.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test exact escaped fixed names, case variants and unknown closed-schema fields while allowing only explicitly defined dynamic keys.
Synthetic core contract cases; Parameterize missing/null/empty/zero and every wrong JSON type; apply only explicitly allowed null/default behavior without coercion.
Synthetic core contract cases; Test every integer lexical form including -0, decimals, exponents, signs and leading zeroes; accept canonical integral tokens only and then apply domain rules.

Synthetic core contract cases; Iterate integer tokens for bounded fields at their exact endpoints and one beyond: port 0, 1, 65535, 65536; rotation_period_seconds 86,399, 86,400, 604,800, 604,801; max_bytes_received 262,144 and 262,145; assert in-range endpoints decode to exactly their decimal value and out-of-range values are rejected. Inject machine-width and floating-point boundary tokens into each integer field: 4294967296 and 4294967297 (2^32, 2^32+1), 9007199254740992 and 9007199254740993 (2^53, 2^53+1), 9223372036854775807 and 9223372036854775808 (2^63-1, 2^63), 18446744073709551617 (2^64+1) and -1 for non-negative fields; assert each is rejected by range or representation, never wrapped, rounded, truncated or clamped to an in-range value. For each bounded integer field, assert both declared domain endpoints are accepted. For each integer field without a finite public upper bound, assert the documented representation maximum is accepted exactly and maximum plus one is rejected. Requirements: REQ-JSON-0007.

Human review case; not automated coverage. Reviewer role: Data-format reviewer (independent of the decoder implementer). Reviewed artifact: Go decoder integer-representation documentation and the field inventory of public integer fields at the reviewed revision. Checklist: (1) Does the documented exact representation for every bounded integer field cover the field's entire declared domain? (2) Is every integer field lacking a finite public upper bound identified, with a documented and reviewed finite exact representation? (3) Does the field inventory used by the automated case include every integer field in the pinned public schemas? Evidence record: A `review` evidence record naming the linked requirement IDs, the reviewed artifact revision, each checklist answer and any finding entered in Specification Issues.

Synthetic core contract cases; After clearMeasurementData deletes replay state with a deterministic clock and fake persistent storage, redeliver previously accepted exact task bytes: an unexpired task is evaluated as new, receives a fresh replay record with unchanged expiry derived from its not_after and creates no record for the cleared acceptance; an expired task is still rejected as task_expired; a failed or incomplete deletion is reported explicitly and leaves no task admitted without replay state. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0024, REQ-TRUST-0025.

Synthetic core contract cases; Present signed remote task packages built from synthetic Ed25519 keys through a fake delivery store, a policy holding two keys of the remote issuer and one of another issuer, and a fake clock, changing one property of an otherwise valid package per case. Assert acceptance for a valid package, a second key of the issuer, a package padded with whitespace to exactly 98,304 bytes, acceptance exactly at not_after, issued_at exactly at not_before and issued_at 300 seconds ahead. Assert task_limit_exceeded for 98,305 bytes; task_policy_unavailable with no installed policy; task_source_unauthenticated for malformed packages (not JSON, a bare task, unknown, duplicate, escaped-duplicate or missing members, wrong member types, padded, standard-alphabet or newline-containing base64url, nonzero trailing bits, an empty task, a 63- or 65-byte signature, fractional, offset, lowercase, leap-second or invalid-date issued_at, invalid identifiers), an unknown key_id, a key of another issuer or a package re-wrapped under another issuer, acceptance one second after not_after, issued_at one second before not_before or after not_after, issued_at 301 seconds ahead, an altered task byte, issued_at, key_id or signature, and a signature over another context or over the bare task; and task_trust_unavailable when trusted time is unavailable at check 6. Assert exactly one class, from the first failing check, for packages failing several checks, and that no rejected package reaches the task codec. A validly signed package whose task is invalid or over 65,536 bytes fails its later step instead. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0043, REQ-TRUST-0046, REQ-TRUST-0047, REQ-TRUST-0048, REQ-TRUST-0049, REQ-TRUST-0050, REQ-TRUST-0052, REQ-LIMIT-0032.

Synthetic core contract cases; Reject six synthetic signed packages that each fail a different verification check (a bad signature, an issuer moved after signing, an unknown key, malformed JSON, issuance one hour ahead and 98,305 bytes), with canaries in the task payload, key IDs, issuers, signature and public-key prefixes and the raw clock error. Assert that each error formats under %v, %+v, %#v and Error() without any canary or the words ed25519, base64, check, key or signature, and that the six errors produce only the two fixed class strings task_source_unauthenticated and task_limit_exceeded, so the failing check cannot be distinguished beyond its class. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0035, REQ-TRUST-0052.

Synthetic core contract cases; Admit a synthetic signed package through a fake delivery store and the test replay store, then assert the replay record holds the remote issuer, the task_id and the SHA-256 digest of the exact task bytes, not of the package, and that neither the record nor the dumped replay store contains the key ID, the encoded signature, the package bytes or the package digest in hex or base64. Assert the remote delivery record no longer resolves after admission, that a package re-signed later over the same task bytes and presented through a new reference resolves to the same admitted identity as a redelivery, and that a package with a corrupted signature leaves no replay record, staged write or resolvable delivery record. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0053.

Synthetic core contract cases; Initialize a client with a generation-2 policy holding two keys of the remote issuer and admit one synthetic task signed with each. Replace it with generation 3 holding only the second key and assert every task handle and queued delivery reference is invalidated, that the task signed with the removed key and a new task signed with it are rejected as task_source_unauthenticated on redelivery, and that the task signed with the retained key resolves to its retained acceptance without a new replay record. Replace it with generation 4 without the remote issuer and assert its handles are invalidated and its packages rejected with no replay write. Assert that a policy whose key names an issuer it does not authorize is not constructed and the active policy is unchanged. With a key valid until one hour after acceptance, admit a task valid for three hours, advance the clock two hours, and assert the handle still resolves with its original expiry while a new presentation of the same package is rejected as task_source_unauthenticated and the handle still resolves after that rejection. With the same key validity, replace the policy after two hours with generation 3 keeping the expired key and assert the handle is invalidated and a redelivery of the same package is rejected as task_source_unauthenticated with no replay write. With an expiring key and a second valid key of the same issuer, advance two hours and assert the same task bytes re-signed with the valid key resolve to the held handle, then after a generation-3 replacement assert the original package is rejected as task_source_unauthenticated and the re-signed package resolves to the retained acceptance as a redelivery with its original expiry and no new replay record. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0030, REQ-TRUST-0051, REQ-TRUST-0054, REQ-TRUST-0055.

finding.selector: heading:GO-SPEC-ISSUE-012: Start of Unacknowledged Bundle Retention

issues.notes: Raised by DEV-563: the public text does not define when the 86,400-second unacknowledged bundle retention starts, or any retention for results not yet in a bundle. No public record exists yet; the disposition awaits public maintainers.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise every replay-table row with a deterministic clock and fake persistent storage: a new replay key continues admission; the same key with identical bytes is idempotent redelivery with no duplicate runs and unchanged expiry; the same key with one changed byte (including whitespace only) is rejected as task_id_conflict; a lower policy generation than the active one is rejected as policy_rollback; an expired task is rejected as task_expired and never reactivated on later redelivery; unavailable or corrupted replay state fails closed with task_trust_unavailable for a remote task and, with the same storage fault injected, for an embedded task, which is never accepted, assigned a handle or made executable without replay state. Assert the persisted record contains only the (issuer_id, task_id) key, a SHA-256 digest equal to an independently computed digest of the exact accepted bytes, the accepted policy generation and acceptance/expiry classes with retention ending 86,400 seconds after task expiry, and that synthetic canary input, target, label, participant and result strings are absent from stored bytes. Post-clearing redelivery rows are planned separately in CC-TRUST-REPLAY-AFTER-CLEARING. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0021, REQ-TRUST-0022, REQ-TRUST-0023, REQ-TRUST-0024, REQ-TRUST-0038, REQ-LIMIT-0023.

Synthetic core contract cases; Initialize with policy generation 2 and admit a task. Assert from the root package source that only the replacement seam assigns the active policy, adapters or admitter, that admission leaves the active generation unchanged and that Initialize on an initialized client returns already_initialized. Drive replacement by quiesce and reinitialization with fault injection at each implemented step. Validation refuses generation 2 (equal) and 1 (lower), an incomplete policy, retained replay acceptances above the new generation, unavailable replay generations and a panicking trusted clock with policy_rejected. After quiescing, a panic while cancelling the current generation and a delivery store that refuses the new generation leave the client uninitialized, and reserved work outliving the lifecycle deadline leaves it blocked with cleanup_incomplete until close. After each validation failure assert the complete generation-2 policy, its handles and its delivery references stay active and its tasks still admit; after each later failure assert no policy remains and that a reinitialized client rejects generation-2 and generation-3 deliveries with task_policy_unavailable, never mixing registrations. Assert in-flight admission is cancelled with no replay record or handle. On a successful generation-3 replacement that removes the task's registration, assert the previous generation's context is cancelled, its task handles and delivery records no longer resolve, a generation-3 redelivery is rejected as target_not_registered and a generation-2 delivery as policy_rollback; after a generation-4 replacement restoring the registration, a redelivery resolves to the retained acceptance under a new handle, and after clearing, initializing generation 2 or 3 fails closed while generation 4 initializes. Send policy-shaped content through permitted task labels and unknown task members and assert the active generation, issuers and registrations are unchanged. Run concurrent replacements and admissions and assert one highest winning generation. Host authentication of policy updates, run cancellation, Network Context cache invalidation and collector, target, proxy and context endpoint paths are planned separately in CC-TRUST-LOCAL-POLICY-LIFECYCLE-RUNTIME. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0029, REQ-TRUST-0030, REQ-TRUST-0031, REQ-TRUST-0032.

Synthetic core contract cases; Admit the same synthetic task bytes through delivery records of each origin: embedded with its issuer and no issued_at is accepted, and remote as a signed package from a trusted key of its issuer, issued at the fake clock, is accepted with a replay digest equal to the digest of the task bytes. For remote origin, remove one input at a time: a remote source with a host-supplied issuer cannot be constructed; the bare task presented as remote without a signed package, and a package with an added authenticated member, are rejected as task_source_unauthenticated; a record presented with package bytes differing by one byte is rejected as task_source_unauthenticated; an unavailable trusted clock is rejected as task_trust_unavailable; no delivery record at all is rejected as task_source_unauthenticated. For every rejection assert no replay or admitted-task record is written. Admission has no transport seam, so zero transport calls are established by checking that the dependency closure of admission contains no network package. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0041, REQ-TRUST-0042, REQ-TRUST-0043, REQ-TRUST-0044.

Synthetic core contract cases; Present signed remote task packages built from synthetic Ed25519 keys through a fake delivery store, a policy holding two keys of the remote issuer and one of another issuer, and a fake clock, changing one property of an otherwise valid package per case. Assert acceptance for a valid package, a second key of the issuer, a package padded with whitespace to exactly 98,304 bytes, acceptance exactly at not_after, issued_at exactly at not_before and issued_at 300 seconds ahead. Assert task_limit_exceeded for 98,305 bytes; task_policy_unavailable with no installed policy; task_source_unauthenticated for malformed packages (not JSON, a bare task, unknown, duplicate, escaped-duplicate or missing members, wrong member types, padded, standard-alphabet or newline-containing base64url, nonzero trailing bits, an empty task, a 63- or 65-byte signature, fractional, offset, lowercase, leap-second or invalid-date issued_at, invalid identifiers), an unknown key_id, a key of another issuer or a package re-wrapped under another issuer, acceptance one second after not_after, issued_at one second before not_before or after not_after, issued_at 301 seconds ahead, an altered task byte, issued_at, key_id or signature, and a signature over another context or over the bare task; and task_trust_unavailable when trusted time is unavailable at check 6. Assert exactly one class, from the first failing check, for packages failing several checks, and that no rejected package reaches the task codec. A validly signed package whose task is invalid or over 65,536 bytes fails its later step instead. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0043, REQ-TRUST-0046, REQ-TRUST-0047, REQ-TRUST-0048, REQ-TRUST-0049, REQ-TRUST-0050, REQ-TRUST-0052, REQ-LIMIT-0032.

Synthetic core contract cases; Reject six synthetic signed packages that each fail a different verification check (a bad signature, an issuer moved after signing, an unknown key, malformed JSON, issuance one hour ahead and 98,305 bytes), with canaries in the task payload, key IDs, issuers, signature and public-key prefixes and the raw clock error. Assert that each error formats under %v, %+v, %#v and Error() without any canary or the words ed25519, base64, check, key or signature, and that the six errors produce only the two fixed class strings task_source_unauthenticated and task_limit_exceeded, so the failing check cannot be distinguished beyond its class. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0035, REQ-TRUST-0052.

Synthetic core contract cases; Admit a synthetic signed package through a fake delivery store and the test replay store, then assert the replay record holds the remote issuer, the task_id and the SHA-256 digest of the exact task bytes, not of the package, and that neither the record nor the dumped replay store contains the key ID, the encoded signature, the package bytes or the package digest in hex or base64. Assert the remote delivery record no longer resolves after admission, that a package re-signed later over the same task bytes and presented through a new reference resolves to the same admitted identity as a redelivery, and that a package with a corrupted signature leaves no replay record, staged write or resolvable delivery record. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0053.

Synthetic core contract cases; Initialize a client with a generation-2 policy holding two keys of the remote issuer and admit one synthetic task signed with each. Replace it with generation 3 holding only the second key and assert every task handle and queued delivery reference is invalidated, that the task signed with the removed key and a new task signed with it are rejected as task_source_unauthenticated on redelivery, and that the task signed with the retained key resolves to its retained acceptance without a new replay record. Replace it with generation 4 without the remote issuer and assert its handles are invalidated and its packages rejected with no replay write. Assert that a policy whose key names an issuer it does not authorize is not constructed and the active policy is unchanged. With a key valid until one hour after acceptance, admit a task valid for three hours, advance the clock two hours, and assert the handle still resolves with its original expiry while a new presentation of the same package is rejected as task_source_unauthenticated and the handle still resolves after that rejection. With the same key validity, replace the policy after two hours with generation 3 keeping the expired key and assert the handle is invalidated and a redelivery of the same package is rejected as task_source_unauthenticated with no replay write. With an expiring key and a second valid key of the same issuer, advance two hours and assert the same task bytes re-signed with the valid key resolve to the held handle, then after a generation-3 replacement assert the original package is rejected as task_source_unauthenticated and the re-signed package resolves to the retained acceptance as a redelivery with its original expiry and no new replay record. Requirements: REQ-TRUST-0030, REQ-TRUST-0051, REQ-TRUST-0054, REQ-TRUST-0055.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise all states/reasons, first termination precedence, measurement presence/absence/partial rules and separation of malformed task errors from results. Interrupt an attempt before and after its test starts and assert not_run before it and incomplete after it (REQ-RESULT-0051), and interrupt it after the test records its terminal outcome and assert the result stays completed with an unchanged state, reason and measurement (REQ-RESULT-0052).

Synthetic core contract cases; Decode synthetic execution objects through the strict task decoder. Reject an execution object without limits. Accept limits as an empty object (registered defaults applied: max_duration_ms 30000, max_bytes_sent 32768, max_bytes_received 131072, max_connections 8) and assert omitted network_path decodes as direct. Accept network_path direct and proxy and reject any other value. Accept network, device and concurrency when absent or present as typed objects of their defined schemas, and reject each when supplied as a non-object (string, array, null) or with an unknown field. Reject an unknown top-level execution field. Requirements: REQ-EXECUTION-0005.

Synthetic core contract cases; Exercise an accepted task with limits max_duration_ms 30000, max_bytes_sent 32768, max_bytes_received 131072 and max_connections 8 on a deterministic clock and scripted transport, with a retry bound permitting a second attempt of the same run. In attempt 1 consume exactly 8 connections, 32,768 application bytes sent and 131,072 received and terminate it with a cross-cutting reason that the public retry rules make retryable. Assert attempt 2 (same run_id, attempt 2) starts with full budgets: it can open 8 connections and send and receive the full byte limits, a 9th connection or one byte beyond either byte limit stops it with resource_limit, and its duration deadline is measured from its own start rather than from attempt 1. Requirements: REQ-EXECUTION-0011.

Synthetic core contract cases; Schedule synthetic tasks on a deterministic clock with scripted transports that record start and end times: two shared tasks S1 and S2 and one exclusive task E, submitted in the orders S1,S2,E and E,S1,S2 and with E submitted while S1 is running. Assert S1 and S2 may overlap, that E's execution interval never overlaps any other measurement's interval, and that no shared task starts while E is active. Assert that when E cannot run alone it either waits or ends not_run per the public constraint-evaluation rules, without starting any network operation while another measurement is active. Requirements: REQ-EXECUTION-0027.

Synthetic core contract cases; Combine task requires_user_consent true and false with a fake host consent provider reporting valid, absent, expired and unavailable consent, and with the local consent requirement off and on. Task true with valid consent: an attempt may start. Task true with absent, expired or unavailable consent: no attempt starts and no Measurement Result is produced. Task false with the local requirement on and absent consent: no attempt starts. Task false with the local requirement off: no consent requirement is added, and risk and target checks still apply.
